name: truthmeter-ai
displayName: TruthMeter AI - Evidence-Based AI Code Metrics
description: How much of your code is AI-written, and does it stick? Measured from git attribution, agent session logs and line survival, not guesses.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: TruthMeter runs git in the workspace, so it only activates in trusted workspaces.

truthmeter.windowDays.description: How many days of git history to analyse.

truthmeter.survival.minAgeDays.description: Only commits at least this old count toward line survival and fix-rate statistics, so recent code has had time to be reworked.

truthmeter.survival.maxFiles.description: Maximum number of files to run git blame on. Files touched least often are skipped first.

truthmeter.agentLogs.enabled.markdownDescription: Read local Claude Code (`~/.claude/projects`) and Codex (`~/.codex/sessions`) session logs to find files an AI agent edited. Only file paths and timestamps inside the workspace are used. Nothing leaves your machine.

truthmeter.attribution.trustCopilotTrail.markdownDescription: Count `Co-authored-by: Copilot` trailers as AI attribution. VS Code's `git.addAICoAuthor` setting can add them automatically, even when Copilot wrote little or nothing.

truthmeter.attribution.customRules.markdownDescription: Extra attribution rules, checked before the built-in ones. Each rule has a `tool` name and a `pattern` (regular expression) tested against the commit author, committer and message.

truthmeter.excludePatterns.description: Regular expressions for file paths to leave out of line counts (lock files, build output).

truthmeter.statusBar.enabled.description: Show the AI-attributed commit share in the status bar.

scripts.test:e2e: npm run compile && npm run bundle && node ./out/test/e2e/runTest.js
scripts.test: npm run lint && npm run test:unit && npm run test:e2e
